requirement:
The bundled skills MUST give authors the following guidance. A
{term}`requirements.references.source_item` that demonstrates a stated structural
obligation SHOULD carry an `{impl}` annotation for the requirement. Mark the
roots from which a reviewer can verify the obligation by following calls, types,
and trait implementations. Helpers reachable from those roots need no separate
marker. Authors MAY add a marker when writing the code or when a structural
reviewer recommends it under {cite}`requirements.authoring.structural_prompt`
and {cite}`requirements.authoring.corrections`.
rationale:
structural: `requirements.references.structural_markers` prescribes the content of the bundled skills' guidance, not how any code is built. It names no library, algorithm, signature, type, field or delegation through a named interface. For each clause, a different implementation would produce the same guidance text and so would still satisfy the requirement:
- "The bundled skills MUST give authors the following guidance" only requires the skill documents to say certain things.
- "SHOULD carry an `{impl}` annotation… Mark the roots from which a reviewer can verify the obligation by following calls, types, and trait implementations. Helpers reachable from those roots need no separate marker." This is advice to authors. Rewording or reorganizing the skill text keeps it satisfied.
- "Authors MAY add a marker when writing the code or when a structural reviewer recommends it" is a MAY, so it imposes nothing to check.

The supplied roots do carry the guidance, although it is not a structural obligation. In `assets/skills/habeas-requirements/SKILL.md`, the "Choosing references" section says to mark roots for stated structural obligations with `{impl}`, and to add the marker when writing the code or on a structural reviewer's recommendation. It also says to leave what a marked root reaches unmarked, and it defines a root as an item that no other `{impl}` item reaches. `assets/skills/habeas-bootstrap-requirements/SKILL.md#section[Bootstrap%20requirements]/section[Tagging]` gives `{impl}` on roots for stated structural obligations, says markers can be added during the inventory or on a structural reviewer's recommendation, and says code a root reaches needs none. The behavioral review can check this wording. No missing implementation root is needed.

behavioral: The requirement obliges the bundled skills to give authors four pieces of guidance. Two marked tests in `tests/authoring_cli.rs` check them by asserting the skill text.

1. A source item that demonstrates a stated structural obligation SHOULD carry `{impl}`. `bundled_skills_direct_the_reference_procedure_and_allow_unmarked_helpers` asserts, in order, that the `habeas-requirements` "Choosing references" section contains "Mark roots for stated structural obligations with `{impl}`".
2. Authors mark the roots a reviewer can verify by following calls, types and trait implementations.
   - `bundled_skills_mark_roots_without_requiring_helper_bookkeeping` asserts the section contains "what an item calls, the types it uses, and the trait methods it calls, transitively" and "Callers don't count".
   - It also asserts the `ROOT` definition: an item that carries out part of a requirement and that no other `{impl}` item for it reaches.
   - It asserts "Roots are per requirement".
3. Helpers reachable from those roots need no separate marker.
   - The same test asserts "Helpers the test calls need nothing", "Leave what a marked root reaches unmarked" and "Don't remove an existing `{impl}` ...".
   - It asserts the gotchas wording "Ordinary functions, types, trait methods, and test helpers need no individual book connection".
   - The first test asserts the `habeas-evidence` wording "Ordinary functions, types, trait methods, and test helpers need no individual book connection" and "Keep meaningful `{impl}` roots and optional explanatory citations".
   - The first test also asserts that the skills don't suggest waivers or catch-all grouping requirements.
4. Authors MAY add a marker when writing the code or when a structural reviewer recommends it. The first test asserts "when writing the code or when a structural reviewer recommends it" in `habeas-requirements`. It asserts "during the inventory or when a structural reviewer recommends it" in `habeas-bootstrap-requirements`. A MAY imposes nothing to check, so this wording is only supplementary.

The tests also check that the other skills refer to the procedure and the root definition rather than restating them. The requirement text doesn't prohibit that restatement, so it adds no obligation.

The test text is mostly in order and uses distinctive phrases, so removing or altering any of this guidance would fail the assertions. I found no unmarked relevant tests and no gaps.

text: :::{req} structural_markers
The bundled skills MUST give authors the following guidance. A
{term}`requirements.references.source_item` that demonstrates a stated structural
obligation SHOULD carry an `{impl}` annotation for the requirement. Mark the
roots from which a reviewer can verify the obligation by following calls, types,
and trait implementations. Helpers reachable from those roots need no separate
marker. Authors MAY add a marker when writing the code or when a structural
reviewer recommends it under {cite}`requirements.authoring.structural_prompt`
and {cite}`requirements.authoring.corrections`.
:::{req} structural_prompt

A non-distributed requirement's structural criterion MUST use the following system and subject messages under {impl}`requirements.ci.review_criteria`. Its behavioral criterion MUST use {cite}`requirements.authoring.initial_prompt` and {cite}`requirements.authoring.behavioral_review`. Each receives the shared declarations and acknowledgments, plus its own review roots. Neither receives the other conversation or its verdict.
```text
# Task
Assess whether implementation roots support the requirement's stated structural obligations.
# Background: Habeas terms
{{habeas_background}}
{{reference_roles}}
# Your task

Identify what the text requires about how the implementation is built. Include required libraries, algorithms, signatures, types, fields, ownership and delegation through named interfaces. For each candidate structural obligation, quote the clause and describe a concrete alternative implementation that preserves the observable behavior but violates that clause. For a prescribed signature or type, consider an alternative declaration that produces the same runtime results. If the alternative still satisfies the text, the implementation choice is discretionary. Finding the code that produces a required output does not by itself create a structural obligation. When every clause specifies only observable behavior, explain why and submit Success even if there are no implementation roots.

Without implementation edges, establish that no structural obligation needs implementation evidence here. Report a missing root when one is needed. Inspect the supplied implementation roots. Follow the calls, types, trait implementations and callbacks needed to map each structural obligation to concrete source. Comments and markers alone do not establish it. Assess obligations delegated to a refining declaration against that declaration's text. Cited declarations supply context. Explain any missing evidence or ambiguity. Leave test adequacy to the behavioral criterion.
# How to judge
{{judgment_rules}}
# Submitting
Submit Success when you find no gap, AcknowledgedGap with entries when every
real gap is acknowledged, and Failed with corrections otherwise. For a missing
{impl} marker, give the role, file and selector in AddReference. In each
marker rationale, quote the clause, describe the behavior-preserving alternative
that violates it, and identify what the reviewer can verify from this root
that is not already covered by the supplied roots and the other proposed roots.
Follow reachable helpers before proposing another marker. Separate callers can
each need a marker when the clause prescribes how each delegates.
For Manual, give the instruction
and explain what gap it closes. Include both when both apply. Cover every
unacknowledged gap. A manual instruction does not acknowledge a gap.
Call submit_result with the chosen variant inside result until it is accepted.
Set result.status to "success", "acknowledged_gap", or "failed".
For a failed result, set each correction's kind to "add_reference" or "manual".
A rejected submission does not complete the assessment. A judgment written in your
reply text is not accepted.
```text
# Subject
Subject: requirement {{subject_name}}
Judge against: the subject's text.
# Review roots
{{review_roots}}
# Acknowledgments
{{acknowledgments}}
# Mandatory inputs
{{mandatory_inputs}}
:::{req} corrections
Each correction in a `Failed` submission MUST be either
`AddReference { role, file, selector, rationale }` or `Manual { instruction, rationale }`.
An `AddReference` proposes a missing `test` or `impl` reference from an existing
item to the assessed definition. Its file MUST be project-relative and its
selector MUST identify that item under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`.
The empty selector identifies the file root. A `Manual` instruction MUST be nonempty and
state what remains to be done.
:::{definition} source_item
:phrase: source item
A node in a project file’s outline, identified by the project-relative path
and an outline selector. For example, `src/auth.rs#fn[check_token]` identifies
a Rust function. The root node represents the whole file. A reference in a
comment belongs to the item that owns the comment under
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`.
